This is the World Values Survey item V4 (Important in life: Family). Family is a highly salient, easily answered item, and across waves 'Don't know' rates for it are very low, typically around 0.2-0.5%.

[0.3]

This is the World Values Survey item (V4 / Q2 "Important in life: Friends"). In WVS, don't know rates for these importance items are typically low, around 0.5-1.5% across countries. For Friends, in wave 6, DK was about 0.8%.

[0.8]

This is the World Values Survey item (V5 in the "Important in life" battery), with Leisure time as one of the domains. For the WVS in the waves covering this item, "Don't know" rates for the importance-of-life-domain items tend to be low, around 1%. Leisure time in particular is easy to answer, so I estimate roughly 1% volunteer "Don't know" across the pooled 60-country sample.

[1.1]

This is the World Values Survey item (Q4 "Important in life: Politics"). Across waves, don't know rates for politics importance are typically around 1-2%; in WVS wave 7 the rate is about 1.5-2%.

[1.7]

This is from the World Values Survey (importance of work, Q5). Don't know rates for the importance-of-life-domains items are typically low, around 1-2% across countries pooled. For work, probably ~1.5%.

[1.4]

This is from the World Values Survey, where "How important is religion in your life" (Q6) has very low non-response. In WVS wave 6, DK for religion importance was around 0.5-1%. Pooled across countries, about 0.6%.

[0.6]

This item comes from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), where "make my parents proud" is a personal-goal item. Don't know rates in WVS for attitudinal items like this tend to be low, around 1-3% on average across countries. This item is relatively easy and personal, so it should be on the lower end.

[1.3]

This item comes from the World Values Survey, which asks whether a pre-school child suffers with a working mother. Across waves and countries, "Don't know" rates on gender-role items like this typically run around 2-4%. Some countries run much higher, and I'd put the pooled figure near 3%.

[3.0]

This is the World Values Survey item on men being better political leaders. DK rates in WVS for this item are typically low, around 2-4% on average across countries, with some countries higher.

[2.6]

This resembles the World Values Survey item "A university education is more important for a boy than for a girl." In WVS, DK rates for this item are typically around 1-3% averaged across countries, with some countries higher. Across waves, the "don't know" proportion for this item is about 2%.

[2.1]

This item is from the World Values Survey ("On the whole, men make better business executives than women do"). Don't know rates in WVS for this item are typically low, around 2-4% on average across countries, with some countries higher.

[3.2]

This is the World Values Survey item "Being a housewife is just as fulfilling as working for pay." Don't know rates in WVS for this item are typically around 2-4% across countries.

[2.9]

This is the World Values Survey item (Q33 in wave 7), where "Don't know" rates are usually low. Across the 60 countries, the typical figure is around 2-4%, and some countries run higher.

[2.6]

This item is from the World Values Survey (jobs scarce: employers should give priority to nation people over immigrants). In WVS wave 7, "Don't know" rates for this item are typically around 3-4% averaged across countries. Given the 5-point scale with a neutral midpoint, DK would be somewhat lower than in the 3-point version used in wave 6, but still non-trivial in some countries.

[3.2]

This is the World Values Survey item "If a woman earns more money than her husband, it's almost certain to cause problems." In WVS wave 7, don't know rates for this item are typically low, about 2-4% on average across countries, with some countries higher. Averaged across 60 countries, I estimate around 3%.

[3.2]

This resembles the World Values Survey item "Homosexual couples are as good parents as other couples" (wave 7), where Don't know rates are typically moderate across many countries, averaging around 4-6% in pooled data. Given the sensitive topic and the 60 countries, the pooled rate is likely about 5%.

[5.0]

This item comes from the ISSP Work Orientations module. In ISSP data, DK rates for attitude items like "People who don't work turn lazy" are typically low, around 1-3% on average across countries, with some countries higher. The middle option "neither agree nor disagree" absorbs much of the uncertainty. Averaged across 60 countries, I'd estimate around 2%.

[2.1]

This item is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), where "Work is a duty towards society" has an agree-disagree scale. Don't know rates across WVS items of this type are typically 2-4% overall, with some countries higher. I estimate about 3%.

[3.0]

This is the World Values Survey item (V137/E047) on basic kinds of attitudes concerning society. In WVS waves, the "don't know" rate for this question is typically relatively high compared to other items, around 6-10% across countries, given the abstract political content.

[7.5]

This is the World Values Survey item about future changes (less importance placed on work). In WVS, DK rates for such items are typically higher than for basic attitudes, around 5-8% across countries.

[6.5]

This is the World Values Survey item on future changes ("greater emphasis on technological development"). Don't know rates in WVS for this item are typically a few percent, averaging around 4-5% across countries, with some countries much higher.

[4.6]

This is a World Values Survey item. Don't know rates for the "future changes" items tend to run higher than for many other WVS items, since respondents find them abstract. For "Greater respect for authority," cross-national DK is roughly 5-8%, so I estimate around 6%.

[6.0]

This is the World Values Survey happiness item. Don't know rates are typically low, around 1% pooled across countries.

[0.9]

This is the World Values Survey item "How much freedom of choice and control you have over the way your life turns out," on a 1-10 scale. In WVS waves, don't-know rates for this item are typically low, around 1-3% on average across countries. Wave 6 shows roughly 1.5-2% don't know on A173, and a few countries run higher.

[1.9]

This looks like the World Values Survey life satisfaction item (Q49). In WVS waves, "Don't know" rates for life satisfaction are typically low, around 1-2% on average across countries, with some countries higher.

[1.3]

This matches the World Values Survey item on satisfaction with financial situation of household. In WVS waves, the "don't know" rate for this item is typically low, around 1-2% overall. Across 60 countries, some countries have higher rates, but the average is probably about 1.5%.

[1.4]

This is a World Values Survey item. Don't know rates for the "gone without enough food" item in the WVS (the "Frequency you/family (last 12 months)" battery) are typically low, around 1-2%.

[1.1]

This resembles the World Values Survey item on going without needed medicine or treatment. Don't know rates for such items in WVS are typically low, around 1-2%, with some variation across countries.

[1.3]

This is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7) item "Gone without a cash income." Don't know rates in WVS for such items are typically low, around 1-3% on average, though some countries run higher. For this particular item, the cross-national average is probably around 2%.

[2.1]

This looks like a World Values Survey item ("Gone without a safe place to live"), with Don't know volunteered in face-to-face interviews. For this type of item, Don't know rates are typically low, around 1%, and I'll go with that.

[0.9]

This looks like the ISSP / World Values-type item on standard of living compared with parents. In cross-national face-to-face surveys, "Don't know" on such a comparison question tends to be low, but across 60 countries (including some with higher non-response) the average is probably around 2-3%.

[2.3]

This is the World Values Survey generalized trust item. Across waves, "Don't know" rates for this question average around 2-3%, varying by country (some higher, e.g., 5-10%).

[2.3]

This is a World Values Survey-style item (trust in family). Non-response for family trust is typically very low, since most people have a clear answer. In WVS, "Don't know" rates for trust in family are roughly 0.5-1.5%.

[0.7]

This is the World Values Survey trust item (V102-ish, "Your neighborhood"). In WVS Wave 6/7, don't know rates for the trust-in-group items are typically around 2-4% for neighborhood, since it's a familiar group. Across 60 countries, the average is probably about 2%.

[2.1]

This is the World Values Survey trust item for people you know personally. Non-response, including "don't know", tends to be very low for this item, since respondents have a clear referent. In WVS Wave 7, the DK rate is around 0.5-1.5%.

[0.9]

This is the World Values Survey trust item ("people you meet for the first time"). Don't know rates in WVS for these items are typically around 2-4% across countries. For "people you meet for the first time," the DK rate is perhaps ~2.5%.

[2.4]

This is the World Values Survey item on trust in people of another religion. In WVS wave 7, "Don't know" rates for these trust items are typically around 2-4%, and the other-religion item is somewhat higher than the personal trust items. Cross-national averages put it at about 3%.

[3.2]

This is the World Values Survey trust-in-other-nationality item. Don't know rates in WVS for these trust items are typically around 2-4% across countries, with the "people of another nationality" item being somewhat higher than personal-trust items.

[3.4]

This looks like World Values Survey confidence in churches. In WVS wave 7, DK rates for confidence items are typically around 2-4% for churches, and the pooled rate across countries is roughly 2-3%.

[2.3]

This is the World Values Survey confidence item for the Armed Forces. In WVS wave 6, "Don't know" rates for the confidence items were generally low, around 2-4%, and for Armed Forces somewhat lower than for items like political parties or the UN. Pooled across 60 countries, I'd estimate roughly 2.5%.

[2.4]

This is the World Values Survey confidence in the press item. Across waves, "Don't know" rates for confidence items are typically around 2-4% on average, with the press being around 2-3%.

[2.6]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence items. For confidence in television, the "Don't know" rate across countries is typically low, around 1-3%, and among the confidence items, television tends to be on the lower end of non-response since most people have an opinion on it.

[1.6]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence-in-institutions battery. Labor unions typically get one of the higher don't-know rates in this battery, because many respondents in low-union-density countries have no clear opinion. Across the WVS waves, the unions item runs around 6-9% don't know, with a pooled estimate near 7%.

[7.5]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence-in-institutions battery. For the police, "Don't know" rates are typically low, around 1-3% across countries, with some countries higher. The pooled average is around 1.5-2%.

[1.7]

This resembles the World Values Survey confidence-in-institutions battery. For the justice system/courts item, the "Don't know" rate across countries typically runs around 3-4%, higher than for more familiar institutions like the church or armed forces.

[3.6]

This resembles the World Values Survey confidence in institutions items. In WVS wave 7, "confidence in the government" has DK rates of roughly 2-3% on average across countries, with some countries higher. Pooled across 60 countries, the DK rate is likely around 2-3%.

[2.5]

This looks like World Values Survey confidence in political parties. DK rates in WVS wave 6/7 for this item are typically around 2-4% on average across countries, with some countries higher. Political parties tends to have a bit higher DK than other institutions.

[3.5]

This resembles the World Values Survey confidence items. Don't know rates for Parliament typically run around 3-5% across countries, with the pooled average perhaps near 4%.

[3.8]

This is from the World Values Survey (confidence in the civil services). Across countries, DK rates for confidence items are typically 2-5%, with civil services somewhat higher than most institutions, since respondents are less familiar with it. In WVS wave 6/7, "Don't know" for civil services averages around 4-5%.

[4.6]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence battery, where "Universities" was added in Wave 7. Don't know rates for the confidence items there are typically 1–5%, and for universities across 60 countries I estimate somewhat higher, around 3–4%, since some respondents are unfamiliar with the institution.

[3.4]

This resembles the World Values Survey (Wave 7) confidence items, where "Don't know" rates for institutional confidence questions typically run 1-5%. For elections, a fairly familiar institution, the rate is likely on the lower side, around 2-3% across countries.

[2.6]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence item for major companies. Across countries, "Don't know" rates for confidence in institutions are typically a few percent, and major companies tends to be somewhat higher than other institutions because respondents may be less familiar with the concept. Pooled across 60 countries, I estimate roughly 4–5%.

[4.5]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence items (Wave 7), where "Don't know" for confidence in banks tends to run a bit higher than for other institutions. Across countries, the average for banks is roughly 3%, with some countries much higher.

[3.2]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence-in-institutions battery, specifically the environmental protection movement item (Wave 6/7). In WVS, DK rates for confidence in organizations like environmental movement tend to be higher than for the police or army, since respondents are less familiar with it. In Wave 6, the DK rate for the environmental organization item was around 5-6%, and in Wave 7 it was probably similar. Across 60 countries, I'd estimate about 5%.

[5.5]

This is a World Values Survey item (confidence in the women's movement), asked in waves 3-6. Don't know rates are higher for less familiar institutions, and the women's movement is unfamiliar in many countries; across countries the pooled DK rate is probably around 8-10%.

[8.5]

This question is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), confidence in charitable or humanitarian organizations. Item non-response (don't know) for confidence items in WVS typically ranges from about 1% to 4%. For charitable organizations, DK rates tend to be a bit higher than for major institutions, perhaps around 3%.

[3.0]

This item is from the World Values Survey confidence battery. For the United Nations, the don't-know rate is typically higher than for domestic institutions, since many respondents lack an opinion. In WVS wave 6/7, DK for the UN runs roughly 5-10% across countries (e.g., higher in some developing countries). Pooled, I estimate around 7%.

[7.0]

This looks like the World Values Survey item on confidence in organizations, where the IMF was included in wave 7 as one of the international organizations. Don't know rates for lesser-known institutions like the IMF are higher than for domestic ones, particularly in lower-income countries, where many respondents are unfamiliar with it. Across 60 countries, I estimate the average volunteered DK rate to be around 15-20%.

[16.5]

This looks like a World Values Survey-style item on confidence in institutions, where the International Criminal Court is a newer and less familiar institution. In WVS Wave 7, DK rates for confidence in international organizations such as the UN, the WTO, and the ICC are typically higher than for domestic institutions. Across 60 countries, awareness of the ICC is limited in many places, so I would estimate the volunteered 'Don't know' share at around 12–15%.

[13.5]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence-in-organizations battery, which included NATO in wave 7. NATO is a more obscure institution than most in that battery, and many respondents in less-engaged countries don't know it, so volunteered "Don't know" rates are fairly high. Across 60 countries I would estimate an average of roughly 10-15%.

[12.5]

This resembles the World Values Survey confidence items, where the World Bank was included in wave 7 (2017-2022) among international organizations. Don't know rates for the UN were around 5-8%, and for less familiar organizations like the World Bank they are higher, since many respondents in developing countries lack familiarity. Across countries, the pooled DK rate for the World Bank is probably around 12-15%.

[13.0]

This looks like the World Values Survey wave 7, which asked about confidence in the WHO. In that wave, don't-know rates were typically higher for international organizations, such as the UN, than for domestic institutions like the police or the armed forces. For the WHO, the share of volunteered "Don't know" answers across 60 countries is probably around 6-8%, with large variation by country; some countries, such as those in South Asia and parts of Africa, run well above that figure. Taking the average across all countries gives roughly 6.5%.

[6.5]

This looks like the World Values Survey confidence-in-organizations battery, where the WTO item has a notably high don't-know rate across countries because many respondents are unfamiliar with it. In WVS wave 7, DK rates for international organizations like the WTO were around 15-25% in many countries, and averaged roughly 15% pooled.

[16.5]

This item resembles those in the World Values Survey / similar cross-national surveys, using a 1-10 scale on an abstract topic (international organizations). Such abstract, unfamiliar trade-off questions typically produce elevated don't-know rates, especially in developing countries. Estimated overall rate is around 10-15%.

[11.5]

This is a knowledge-type question (which country is a permanent UNSC member, with India being the incorrect option; likely a "which of these" item). Knowledge questions in cross-national face-to-face surveys typically yield higher DK rates, and the format here (three options read aloud, pick one or possibly multiple) leaves room for volunteered DK among respondents who are unsure. I estimate about 12%.

[12.0]

This looks like a knowledge question (World Values Survey-style, probably a knowledge/awareness item). Knowledge questions tend to elicit higher DK rates, especially in cross-national samples with lower-awareness populations. Since DK isn't read aloud but volunteered, the rate is moderate. I estimate around 12%.

[12.0]

This is the World Values Survey membership item for art, music, educational organizations. Don't know rates in WVS for these membership items are typically low, around 1-2% on average across countries.

[1.3]

This appears to be the World Values Survey membership question. In the WVS, DK rates for organization membership items are typically low, around 1-3%, with political party membership perhaps slightly higher in some countries. Averaged across 60 countries, I'd estimate roughly 1.5%.

[1.4]

This is the World Values Survey organizational membership item. In WVS, DK rates for these membership items are typically low, around 1-2%, though they vary across countries. For charitable/humanitarian organization, the pooled DK is probably around 1.5%.

[1.4]

This item comes from the World Values Survey organizational membership battery. For these items, "Don't know" is volunteered rarely, typically around 1-3% across countries, and perhaps a bit higher for less familiar organization types such as self-help groups.

[1.6]

This is the World Values Survey item (E035), a 10-point scale. Don't know rates across waves typically run about 3-6% on average across countries.

[4.3]

This is the World Values Survey item (E036). Don't know rates across countries on this item are typically around 5-8% on average. In WVS wave 6, E036 DK averages about 6-7%. Some countries have much higher rates.

[6.5]

This is the World Values Survey item (E037) on government vs individual responsibility, on a 1-10 scale. Across WVS waves, DK rates for this item are typically around 3-5% on average, higher in some countries.

[3.6]

This is the World Values Survey item (E039) "Competition good or harmful," a 10-point scale. Don't know rates in WVS for such attitude items typically run 3-6% overall, and this one tends to be somewhat higher than the ideology items, at around 4-5%.

[4.3]

This is the World Values Survey item (E040). Don't know rates in WVS for such 10-point scale items are typically around 2-4% overall, with some countries higher.

[2.8]

This is the World Values Survey item (V81 in wave 5/6 – "Protecting environment vs. economic growth"). Don't know rates across countries are typically around 2-4% on average, with some countries higher. In WVS wave 6, the DK rate for this item is approximately 3%.

[3.1]

This looks like the World Values Survey item (E120-type corruption perception). Across WVS countries, don't-know rates on this item are typically a few percent, with some countries much higher.

[4.5]

This is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), "Corruption: State authorities." Don't know rates for these items are typically around 5-8% across countries, higher in some places.

[6.5]

This is from the World Values Survey wave 7 corruption perception items (e.g., "How many of the following people do you think are involved in corruption?"). The business executives item typically has a higher DK rate than the others, in the range of roughly 6-8% across countries.

[6.5]

This looks like the World Values Survey item on perceived corruption among local authorities. In WVS wave 7, "Don't know" rates for these corruption items are typically a few percent. Local authorities likely have a somewhat higher DK rate than the state authorities, around 4-5% overall.

[4.6]

This resembles the World Values Survey item on perceived corruption among civil service providers. Don't-know rates in the WVS for this type of item are typically moderate, since respondents may feel unfamiliar with the subject, and the cross-national average tends to land around 6-8%.

[6.5]

This resembles the World Values Survey wave 7 corruption perception items ("How many of the following people do you think are involved in corruption?"). For categories like journalists and media, "don't know" rates tend to be relatively higher than for politicians. Across 60 countries, the average is probably around 6-8%.

[6.5]

This looks like an item from the World Values Survey, where a "Hard to say" option is offered explicitly as a substantive choice, so "Don't know" would be volunteered only rarely. The statement "women are less corrupt than men" is somewhat unusual, and some respondents would still say they don't know, but a good share of them would likely pick "Hard to say" instead.

Typical WVS "don't know" rates for opinion items run around 2-5%, and for this question I'd expect volunteered "Don't know" to be a bit lower than that. I'll estimate about 3%.

[3.2]

This appears to be from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), item on perceived risk of being held accountable for giving or receiving a bribe. Don't know rates for such items are typically moderate, around 5-8% across countries, higher in some.

[6.5]

This looks like the World Values Survey item "Impact of immigrants on the development of the country." In the WVS, DK rates for this item vary across countries, usually in the range of 3-10%, with higher rates in some countries. The pooled rate across 60 countries is probably around 5-6%.

[5.5]

This looks like a WVS-style item. The substantive options include "Hard to say" explicitly, which absorbs much of the uncertainty, so volunteered "Don't know" is likely modest. Across 60 countries, WVS DK rates for immigration items are typically around 3-6%.

[4.5]

This item has a "Hard to say" substantive middle option, which absorbs many uncertain respondents, so volunteered "Don't know" would be lower than on typical attitude items. Across 60 countries, including some with low familiarity with immigration, it likely runs at a few percent.

[3.5]

This item comes from the World Values Survey wave 7, where the "Hard to say" option is explicitly offered, which absorbs many uncertain respondents. Volunteered "Don't know" is then residual. In WVS-7, DK rates for items like this are typically around 3-6% across countries, with some countries much higher.

[4.5]

This looks like an item from the Values Surveys' immigration battery (EVS/WVS), whose "Don't know" rates are typically in the 3-8% range. Because "Hard to say" is offered as a substantive middle option, that probably absorbs some of the uncertainty that would otherwise be recorded as "Don't know." Even so, a question about political refugees may be harder for respondents in many countries, and across 60 countries the volunteered "Don't know" rate probably runs a little higher. I estimate about 5%.

[5.0]

This is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), where the item on immigration and terrorism has substantive options including "Hard to say" in the middle. Because that middle category is offered, volunteered "Don't know" is typically modest, though across 60 countries it can be higher in some places. I estimate around 3-4% on average.

[3.6]

This looks like a World Values Survey item (Wave 7) on immigration effects. Substantive options include a "Hard to say" middle option, which absorbs some uncertainty, but "Don't know" is still recorded in WVS at modest rates. Across 60 countries, the DK rate for such attitudinal items is typically around 3-5%, and for this immigration item it may be a bit higher in some countries.

[4.5]

This looks like the World Values Survey-style item on immigration, with a "Hard to say" option offered explicitly. Since a middle category is read aloud, volunteered "Don't know" is typically modest, though it varies across 60 countries. I estimate it at around 4%.

[4.2]

This looks like a World Values Survey-type item on immigration effects. The question has an explicit "Hard to say" middle option, which absorbs many uncertain respondents, so volunteered "Don't know" is usually lower. Across 60 countries in a face-to-face mode, typical DK rates for attitude items run around 3-6%.

[3.8]

This looks like the World Values Survey item on immigration policy, where "Don't know" is recorded if volunteered and not read aloud. In WVS waves, the don't-know rate for this item across countries is typically around 3-5%, with higher rates in some countries.

[4.0]

This is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7) item on neighborhood security: "How frequently do the following things occur in your neighborhood: robberies." In WVS-7, don't know rates for the items in this battery were generally low but notable, around 2-4%. Robberies might be slightly higher than others, such as alcohol consumption in the streets. I estimate about 3%.

[3.2]

This looks like the World Values Survey Wave 7 neighborhood security item ("Alcohol consumed in the streets"). Don't know rates in WVS for such items are typically around 2-4%, and for this item, with varied countries, perhaps ~3%.

[3.0]

This is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7) security/crime items: "Frequency in your neighborhood: Police or military interfere with people's privacy." DK rates on these items tend to be modest but higher than typical attitudinal questions, since respondents may be unsure. In WVS7, the neighborhood items (e.g., robberies, alcohol consumed in streets, police interference) had DK around 3-6%.

[4.5]

This is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), where items on neighborhood crime and security include "Racist behavior." Don't know rates for such items across WVS are typically in the low single digits, with racist behavior having somewhat higher non-response than other items since it requires judgment about neighbors. I estimate about 3%.

[3.2]

This item is from the World Values Survey (Wave 7), on neighborhood crime frequency, including street drug sales. In WVS7, "don't know" rates for these neighborhood items tend to be modest, with drug sale items somewhat higher than others, as some respondents are unaware. I estimate around 4-5%.

[4.6]

This resembles the World Values Survey (wave 7) question about neighborhood security. For the items on "Frequency in your neighborhood: Street violence and fights," the 'Don't know' rate is typically low, around 2-3% on average across countries.

[2.3]

This looks like the World Values Survey Wave 7 item on how frequently things occur in the neighborhood (Q82-type items, e.g., sexual harassment). Don't know rates for these items are typically a few percent; sensitive topics like sexual harassment tend to have a higher DK rate, around 4-6% across countries.

[4.8]

This is from the World Values Survey, which asks about things done for reasons of security, including avoiding going out at night. Don't know rates for these yes/no behavioral items are typically low, roughly 1-2%, but vary across countries.

[1.3]

This looks like a World Values Survey item ("Things done for reasons of security: carried a knife, gun or other weapon"). It is a simple yes/no behavioral question, and "Don't know" is generally low for such items, though sensitive items may see a bit more. Typical DK rates in WVS for this battery are around 1-2%.

[1.3]

This is the World Values Survey wave 7 item (Q142 and neighbors on worries). In WVS7, "Don't know" rates for these worry items are typically low, around 1-3%. The job-loss worry item likely has somewhat higher non-response because some respondents (retired, not employed) find it less applicable, so I estimate about 2%.

[2.0]

This looks like the World Values Survey item (Wave 6) on worries, including "not being able to give one's children a good education." In WVS, DK rates for this item are typically low, around 2-4%, with the "not applicable"/no children cases perhaps contributing some. The cross-national average is probably around 2.5%.

[2.6]

This is a simple factual yes/no question about a respondent's own experience (World Values Survey-style). Don't know responses are typically low for such questions, around 0.5-1%.

[0.6]

This looks like the World Values Survey item on whether the respondent's family was a victim of a crime in the past year. Item non-response on this is generally low, since it is a straightforward factual question. In WVS data, "Don't know" rates for this item are typically around 0.5-1.5% across countries, and the pooled figure is likely around 1%.

[0.9]

This looks like the World Values Survey wave 7 item (Q142 "worries: a terrorist attack"). In WVS7, DK rates for these worry items are generally low, around 1-3%. For terrorist attack, I recall approximately 2%.

[2.1]

This item resembles the World Values Survey wave 7 question on worries (job loss, war, terrorist attack, civil war). In WVS, "Don't know" rates for such items are usually low, around 1-3%, though they are higher in some countries. For the civil war item, I'd estimate an average of about 2-3% across countries.

[2.3]

This looks like the World Values Survey item "Freedom and Equality - Which more important" (E-series). In WVS, don't know rates for this item are typically around 3-5% across countries. In wave 6 it's roughly 3%.

[3.4]

This item looks like it comes from the World Values Survey. Across countries, volunteered "Don't know" on a forced-choice item like this is typically low, but because the question is abstract, some respondents decline to choose. Rates likely range from near 0 to around 10% in some countries, with a pooled average in the low single digits.

[2.6]

This item matches the World Values Survey question "Of course, we all hope that there will not be another war, but if it were to come to that, would you be willing to fight for your country?" Across waves, "Don't know" responses to it are fairly common, roughly 5-8% pooled, and higher in some countries (e.g., Japan, Germany, and several others).
